answer: A pearl grows one verified layer at a time, and so should trust: an identity starts thin and earns a thicker pearl only after peer-checked work, each layer signed by a different honest counterparty. A spiral check traces the pearl's history outward — a new claim needs confirmation from witnesses a ring further out, so a fake cluster's rings all point back to the same few creators. An anchor deposit locks funds to one hardware key per identity, forfeited if any ring contradicts the pearl. A sybil must fund dozens of slow-growing pearls, costing more than the trust any one can borrow.
